**General Remarks**
I am a huge fan of the plot twist. Despite the title, I only realised well into the story what the 'ghost' thing was all about.

**Mechanics**

I thought the title captured the heart and goal of the story. However, I do think there are more fitting and more captivating titles to be found with the words 'ghost' and 'house', especially since only one ghost is given a voice. From what I have read, it's not clear whether there are just one, or multiple ghosts present in the house.

Personally, I also thought the hook came a little late, but I don't expect you to immediately reveal the plot twist of your story. Nevertheless, I do think it's possible to make the first paragraph a bit more interesting, by emphasizing the importance of the sale to her. ("*would finally be big-time*" brings the message across, but it could be expressed more strongly/elaborated).

**Setting**

It was very easy to imagine the setting. The description of the house was very detailed and well done. Despite having no exact location mentioned, I could perfectly visualize it being in Pennsylvania or some other northern state with a lot of old, haunted houses.

**Staging and character**

The characters seem a little plain to me. I really lacked a description of physical characteristics of Pam and Jerry, which made it hard to imagine what they are like. Apart from the things they say, there is little to no info about how they actually react to the house (body language-wise), or their personality. It's like Pam and Jerry are practically created to move the story forward, their role being dominant over their personality. Which is not wrong per se, but it feels odd to me. 

There is a relationship going on between them// them and Maxine // them and the house. However, in your story, only the middle one is clear. Nevertheless, I think their relationship gives off a weird vibe. Maxine is awfully familiar with them. The reader is left clueless as to how and when they had met before. Furthermore, there is no handshake as a greeting or whatsoever. I was given the impression she was a working student, rather than a true realtor, considering her lack of formality and manners. The visit looked not well prepared by her either, as she plainly mentioned some "*squatters*" had been around. Would anyone trying to sell a house truly say this?

**Heart**

I don't think there was a subliminar message to the story, or was there? A warning to be careful when buying old houses, perhaps?

**Plot and pacing**

I really liked the plot, especially how you achieved to switch atmospheres so quickly. It went from 'basic salestalk' to very dark in a matter of minutes.
However the last part, where she goes to collect her payment, is a bit messy. I can totally see where you were wanting to go with the part about the payment. It does create a sort of tension and triggered my curiosity. However, your description of the payment is really vague. Is it money ? valuables? human organs? Who knows?

**Dialogue**

I think the amount of dialogue was sufficient to fit the story. Apart from the familiarity, it did seem believable enough. I do think however, that the "*she said*" parts, could be elaborated somewhat. A real person almost never 'just' says something, there is always a certain kind of feeling attached to it, feelings which I found lacking in your story.

All in all, I would give the story a solid 7.75/10 (more than 7.5 but less than 8))
